full_judgment:
5. I have heard the learned Advocates of both side, perused the records of the case and the impugned order. From the records it appears that the petitioners filed the application on 30-4-92 for addition of parties under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the instant suit stating, inter alia, that though the plaintiff filed the suit claiming that the suit land is owned and possessed by one Kalu in his 16 annas share but the petitioners claimed that the suit land was actually owned and possessed by Nalu who was the father of Kalu. The jote of Nalu within the mouza Punail under Khatian Nos.125 and 1271, the lands of Nalu within mouza No.29 Delua under Maliki Khatian No.5 and the other lands within mouza No.35 Bara Paila under Khatian No.81. The petitioners claimed that the lands of those 4(four) Khatians belonged to Nalu, the father of Kulu and the petitioners are the co-sharers and possessors of those lands of aforesaid four Khatians (jotes) of Nalu by way of inheritance, purchase and gift. But the plaintiffs, without bringing into hotchpotch of those lands brought the suit and without making the petitioners parties therein and in view of the specific claim of the petitioners I am of the view that they are the necessary parties to be added in this suit in question for adjudicating upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit effectually and completely and without deciding such question no decree can be passed. On perusal of the impugned order it does not reflect as to how the court below considered the alleged claim of the petitioners and misdirected himself in holding that the petitioners have not stated any thing about their community of interest in the land of Kalu without noticing the fact that Kalu is the son of Nalu and the petitioners put forward the claim over the land of Nalu and not the land of Kalu. The fact remains that since the petitioners claimed their subsisting right, title and interest over the land belonged to Nalu, there should be complete adjudication of the same. Mrs. Sofia Khatoon though argued that the petitioners were made parties in the Civil Revision No.324 of 1989 but she could not show me as to whether all the petitioners herein were made parties therein. It has been stated in the counter affidavit to the effect that "In the said Civil Revision No.324 of 1989 the present petitioner was made party, the notice was duly served but the petitioner did not appear and contest" But be that as it may, the fact remains that the petitioners were not made parties in the suit itself. 

 7. In a partition suit even a third person, claiming title to property adverse to plaintiff and defendant is necessary party and in the instant case the petitioners claim to be co-sharers by way of inheritance by purchase and gift etc. In the disputed 4 Khatians of Nalu, father of Kalu and the petitioners cannot but be necessary parties and there is an exceptional circumstances under which addition of parties can be allowed even after preliminary decree is passed. Having regard to the above discussions and in the fact and circumstances I hold that the impugned order suffers from legal infirmity and it is set aside.
